# Code review: `253dd40…HEAD` (Linear release workflow)

**Mode:** full review of the committed range `253dd40 → 5506983` (3 commits, 1 file, +121 −0). I edited nothing, installed nothing, ran no tests, and posted nothing.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Verdict** | ✅ Ready to open |
| **Score** | 100 across 4 scored areas (1 finding checked, 0 held up strongly enough to count) |
| **Held the score down** | Nothing |
| **Fix first** | Nothing blocks. One low-confidence observation below is worth a look. |

## Scores by area

| Area | Score | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Security | 100 | Checked 10 applicable rules. Inputs reach the script through `env:`, both actions are pinned to a full SHA, permissions are `{}` at workflow level and `contents: read` for the job, and checkout uses the resolved tag. |
| Bugs | 100 | 1 raw finding; it scored below the counting threshold (see below). |
| Conventions | 100 | SPDX header, R-030 SHA pinning with a version comment, naming, secrets handled like the other workflows, `ci:` commit subjects. |
| KISS | 100 | No surplus structure. All three step outputs are used, and the comments match what the code does. |
| Regression, Testing, Performance, DRY, Architecture | n/a | The workflow is new and standalone. It changes no existing behaviour, has no test harness, touches no hot path, duplicates nothing, and changes no layer boundaries. |

## What this review did not cover

- **The Linear action's inputs weren't checked.** The network was blocked, so I couldn't confirm that `linear/linear-release-action@3858a5d…` (v0.14.6) accepts the input names `access_key`, `command`, `version`, `links` and `dry_run`. If one is misspelled, it may be ignored silently. Check against the action's `action.yml`.
- **No linter ran.** actionlint, zizmor and shellcheck aren't installed, so there was no static lint of the workflow.
- **No run comparison.** No "since your last run" section, because I wrote nothing under `.git/` in a read-only review.

## Must fix before opening
None.

## Worth a ticket
None.

## Not sure about this one (low confidence, not scored)

**`.github/workflows/linear-release.yml:39`: runs for the same release can land in different concurrency groups**
- **What happens:** the workflow-level `concurrency.group` is built from the raw trigger values, before the `Resolve release` step (`:54-100`) normalizes the version:
  - A published release gets `linear-release-v1.122.0`.
  - A manual run with `1.122.0`, a format the input description at `:27` suggests, gets `linear-release-1.122.0`.
  - A manual run with no version gets `linear-release-refs/heads/main`.
- **Effect:** those runs don't queue behind each other, so two `sync` calls for the same release can run at once.
- **How it was judged:**
  - One agent confirmed the mechanism but only partly: whether the Linear action is safe under concurrent calls couldn't be checked without its source.
  - The other called it weakened. Re-syncing is the workflow's documented repair path (`:13-14`), so the likely cost is a duplicate API call, not lost data. The race also needs a manual run to overlap an automatic one.
  - Final rating: low impact, low likelihood, confidence about 20–35 (below the counting threshold of 40).
- **The commit message doesn't cover it.** `5506983` explains why unversioned manual runs share a group, but not the `v`-prefix mismatch.
- **If you want to fix it:** the fix the reviewer suggested doesn't work, because GitHub Actions expressions have no `substring`. What does work is splitting the workflow into two jobs:
  - a `resolve` job that outputs the normalized `tag`;
  - a `sync` job with `needs: resolve` and a job-level `concurrency: group: linear-release-${{ needs.resolve.outputs.tag }}`.

## Checked and ruled out (no finding)

- **Error annotation (`:72`).** `::error::` echoes the raw input, but only people with write access can start the workflow, and the old workflow commands that could be abused this way are disabled on the runner.
- **Checkout credentials (`:104-108`).** They are kept by default, the same as every other workflow in the repo. The token only has `contents: read`.
- **Release URL lookup (`:92`).** When no release exists for the tag, `|| true` leaves `URL` empty, never the literal string `null`.
- **Latest-release lookup (`:77`).** It fails with gh's raw error instead of the friendlier message at `:81`. Only the wording differs; the run still fails correctly.
- **`dry_run` fallback (`:121`).** `inputs.dry_run || false` evaluates to `false` on the release trigger.
- **Fail-open (`:114`).** Both triggers behave as documented.
- **History for the scan (`:105-108`).** `fetch-depth: 0` with a tag checkout fetches full history and all tags.

## Worth tidying
No proposals. The file is new and already follows the patterns of the other workflows.

## How this was produced
- Three category passes ran in parallel: security, bugs, and conventions with KISS.
- The one raw finding got an independent validator (PARTIAL) and refuter (WEAKENED).
- Tally: 1 of 1 checked by both agents; 0 confirmed, 1 contested with confidence under 40, 0 ruled out.
